summary: Operations/source review of cb438d1083e9ae3e2a38dd8e5d7dba4c778b2e89 found two PostgreSQL failure-handling defects. An isolated wire-protocol mock reproduced process exit on idle connection loss and pending connection/pool work without default application deadlines. Hosted capacity, identity/provider integration and recovery remain unverified deployment gates; the local Compose file is explicitly a demo.
limitations: No actual Google Workspace, Cloudflare, cloud compute, PostgreSQL service or object-store tenant was accessed. Candidate Cloud Run/Cloud SQL/R2 integration, TLS, IAM, SSE/proxy behavior and recovery are not validated.

Mock reproductions used local Node v26.0.0 and installed pg 8.23.0; Docker declares Node 22. Reproduce failure/recovery checks in the final immutable runtime image before accepting a fix. The mocks use synthetic local identity only and contain no real credentials.

This was one bounded independent source review. Shared full suites/builds were reserved for the lead, so this node makes no assertion that they passed. No sustained capacity, OS-image vulnerability scan, actual database restart, restore drill or production SLO measurement was run.

Dependency advisories came from lead-generated audit artifacts. Development packages are shipped by Docker, but no remotely reachable vulnerable call path was established. See deployment-notes.json for release hygiene and counterevidence.

Existing runtime health evidence describes an older deployed revision, not the reviewed HEAD. Repository documentation explicitly leaves hosted environment, ownership, retention, real user acceptance and measured RPO/RTO open.
